sketch: Goal: approximate a target single-qubit unitary U within epsilon using a Repeat-Until-Success (RUS) circuit over Clifford+T with one ancilla and a measurement. Reconstruction scope (assumed): one tiny instance, U = R_z(theta) with a fixed theta, built as a single RUS attempt that is a measurement-free unitary on 2 qubits (system q0, ancilla q1). Steps: (1) Prepare the ancilla in |0> and the system in an arbitrary input state. (2) Apply a fixed Clifford+T sequence W on system+ancilla, for example H on the ancilla, controlled-style Clifford+T blocks, T and T-dagger gates, and a closing H on the ancilla. (3) The ancilla outcome 0 is the success branch. Its Kraus operator K0 = (I tensor <0|) W (I tensor |0>) acts on the system as a non-unitary operator proportional to a unitary V with V close to U. Specifically, the entries of K0 are of the form (a + b*sqrt2)/2^k-style Z[1/sqrt2, i] numbers, with K0 = c*V where c is a scalar of modulus less than 1 and is the square root of the success probability. A failure outcome gives a known Kraus operator K1 that is a Clifford+T-correctable operator (or the system is corrected by a fixed Clifford so the attempt can be retried). (4) Classical search, which is probabilistically polynomial: randomly sample candidate Gaussian-integer-like numbers in Z[1/sqrt2, i] (norm-equation or Diophantine-type constraints) to build the candidate entries, check that the resulting 2x2 operator has a valid RUS completion (the complementary block unitarity constraint |u|^2+|v|^2 constraints met via a norm-equation solve using randomized factoring), and keep those with ||V - U|| <= epsilon. This randomized selection replaces the exponential exhaustive enumeration. (5) Compile the chosen operator into a Clifford+T circuit with one ancilla; the expected T-count is T_per_attempt divided by the success probability, which can fall below the ancilla-free 3 log2(1/epsilon) bound because a non-unitary success operator allows a finer approximation per T gate. For the runner, only the single attempt unitary W is built, with the success branch defined by projecting the ancilla on |0>; the measurement and the retry loop are handled in classical postprocessing outside the circuit.
